steps.prompt:

1. Replace the bear in Image 1 with the character identity from Image 2 as faithfully as possible. Preserve the exact source proportions: large round head, original large vertical oval eyes with their white rims and brown pupils, small brown nose, two curved smiling muzzle lines with the outer muzzle arch and pink tongue, original round ears and short arms/legs. Coral-red beret, pale-yellow body, warm brown outline, no blush. Do not make a generic redesigned teddy or reduce the eyes. Full body and beret remain visible. 2. REMOVE the decorative gold sparkle stars and orange accent strokes near the bear and placard. Count 128 is an ordinary counting moment, not a ten-count milestone. Calm sky and clear space are important.

5. Keep count "128" crisp, not clipped or hidden. No other words, numbers, controls, logos or watermark.
Use the same soft paper/watercolor garden world, turquoise sky and lime grass, but keep the current composition. This is a visual-reference image only; no video or audio.

Create ONE clean high-resolution landscape storyboard sheet with EXACTLY SIX equal panels in a 3-column by 2-row grid. Each panel contains a 16:9 counting-video frame with captions BELOW the frame, outside the video. Warm cream sheet, dark brown readable Japanese type. Prefer 2560x1440 or larger. Spend the space on legible frames and notes, not decorative borders.

Reference roles:
Image 1 = corrected keyframe layout/style: same garden, bear LEFT, cream wood number board RIGHT, flower progress BOTTOM, separate small range pill ABOVE.
Image 2 = canonical bear identity. Preserve red beret, pale-yellow body, large vertical oval eyes with white rims, brown outlines, nose/muzzle/tongue, original proportions. No blush, no generic teddy redesign. Keep the same bear design in every panel.
Image 3 = garden prop reference for the yellow flying bird and soft rainbow.
Image 4 = the cream/coral toy airplane reference; use ONE plane, not the two-pose atlas.
Image 5 = white cloud reference; use cloud only, no rain or other atlas objects.
Never put an atlas, reference labels, or black transparency background inside the storyboard.
